main.title: The Beatles: Rock Band
main.subtitle: The Beatles’ musical history becomes a performance to share
main.summary: Harmonix built a dedicated Beatles game around the band’s recordings, historic venues, three-part vocal harmonies and imaginative studio dreamscapes.

cards.heading: From the Cavern Club to the rooftop
cards.text: Released worldwide on September 9, 2009 for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Wii, The Beatles: Rock Band follows the group through 45 songs on the original disc. Harmonix developed the game with Apple Corps’ involvement, with MTV Games publishing and Electronic Arts distributing it. The story moves through recognisable moments and places in the band’s career, including the Cavern Club, the Ed Sullivan Show, Shea Stadium, Budokan and the Apple rooftop. Costumes, instruments and performances change with the period.

cards.heading: Three voices in harmony
cards.text: The familiar guitar, bass and drum parts are joined by support for three-part vocal harmonies. Up to six people can perform together when three singers join the instrumental players. Singing is not simply another coloured lane: several voices can follow distinct pitches at the same time. Training modes let players practise those relationships. The game also avoids some of the intrusive sounds used elsewhere in Rock Band, allowing the Beatles’ recordings to remain at the centre of the experience.

cards.heading: Making the studio years visible
cards.text: For the studio years, the band moves from Abbey Road into animated dreamscapes inspired by the songs. These are artistic interpretations rather than reconstructions of concerts that never happened. Giles Martin served as music producer, helping adapt the original recordings for an interactive mix. Additional Beatles songs and albums were later offered as downloadable content, separate from the original 45-song disc selection. The dedicated game remains a distinct interpretation of the band’s work, rather than a general Rock Band expansion.

main.title: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver
main.subtitle: Johto returns with a partner walking beside the trainer
main.summary: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver remake Gold and Silver for Nintendo DS. Game Freak returned to Johto with new presentation, a Pokémon following the trainer and the bundled Pokéwalker accessory. Released in Japan on 12 September 2009, the paired games begin with Professor Elm's first partner and grow into a journey across Johto and Kanto.

cards.heading: Two regions remembered
cards.text: Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver remake Gold and Silver for Nintendo DS. Game Freak returned to Johto with new presentation, a Pokémon following the trainer and the bundled Pokéwalker accessory. Released in Japan on 12 September 2009, the paired games begin with Professor Elm's first partner and grow into a journey across Johto and Kanto.

cards.heading: Company on the path
cards.text: The leading Pokémon walks behind the player outside its Poke Ball. Turning to speak to it gives a familiar team member a presence between battles, whether the partner is small enough to fit beside the trainer or towers over the path. That company changes how repeated travel feels. The route to a Gym, a return through a town and a pause near the water all include a creature the player has chosen and raised.

cards.heading: A journey carried in a pocket
cards.text: The Pokéwalker carries one partner beyond the DS. Infrared communication transfers a Pokémon to the small pedometer, where walking supports progress and opens opportunities to find items or meet other creatures. Returning to the cartridge brings those discoveries back into the main adventure. The accessory ties a portable game to an ordinary day's movement, giving the idea of travelling with a Pokémon a small physical object to accompany it.

cards.heading: A team for another kind of contest
cards.text: The Pokéathlon gives a team another kind of challenge. Three Pokémon enter athletic events whose courses test qualities such as speed, power and jumping. Choosing the right combination matters because a strong battler may suit a different sport from a quick or agile partner. Events award points that can be exchanged for prizes, adding another reason to look closely at the abilities of creatures already travelling with the player.

main.title: Endless Ocean 2: Adventures of the Deep
main.subtitle: The next dive reaches further
main.summary: Endless Ocean 2: Adventures of the Deep is Arika's Wii diving sequel, released in North America as Endless Ocean: Blue World. Its journey expands beyond the original game's sea to destinations around the world, including polar and freshwater environments. Exploring, identifying animals and recovering objects remain central activities, now connected with a larger range of places and a continuing story. The change gives the diving routine more variety: preparing for a particular destination also means considering the different creatures and conditions that may be encountered below its surface.

cards.heading: The next dive reaches further
cards.text: Endless Ocean 2: Adventures of the Deep is Arika's Wii diving sequel, released in North America as Endless Ocean: Blue World. Its journey expands beyond the original game's sea to destinations around the world, including polar and freshwater environments. Exploring, identifying animals and recovering objects remain central activities, now connected with a larger range of places and a continuing story. The change gives the diving routine more variety: preparing for a particular destination also means considering the different creatures and conditions that may be encountered below its surface.

cards.heading: An encounter may need some care
cards.text: Some creatures can now pose a danger, and the Pulsar provides a way to calm them through electrical charges. The same tool can help sick or injured animals, giving it a role beyond protecting the diver. Oxygen and equipment also affect the practical limits of an expedition. Salvaged objects can be sold to finance upgrades and other purchases. These additions give preparation a clearer place in the adventure, connecting what is found during one dive with the equipment and opportunities available when setting out on the next one.

cards.heading: The collection continues above the water
cards.text: The aquarium returns with areas for different kinds of wildlife, including smaller creatures and species associated with the shore. Dolphins can again become companions, and the diver can ride them to move through the water. A private reef and island decorations provide other ways to shape the spaces visited between expeditions. These activities give discoveries a home outside the moment of identification. The player can return from a distant location with more than a completed route, gradually building a collection of animals, objects and places that records the longer journey.

main.title: Halo 3: ODST
main.summary: Halo 3: ODST is a 2009 first-person shooter video game developed by Bungie and published by Microsoft Game Studios.

cards.heading: Searching New Mombasa
cards.text: Halo 3: ODST is a 2009 first-person shooter video game developed by Bungie and published by Microsoft Game Studios. The fifth installment in the Halo franchise, it was released on the Xbox 360 in September 2009. Players assume the roles of United Nations Space Command Marines, known as "Orbital Drop Shock Troopers" or ODSTs, during and after the events of Halo 2 and before the events of Halo 3. In the game's campaign mode, players explore the ruined city of New Mombasa, to discover what happened to their missing teammates in the midst of the Covenant alien invasion of Earth. In the "Firefight" cooperative multiplayer option, players battle increasingly difficult waves of enemies to score points and survive as long as possible. The game also contains the entirety of Halo 3's multiplayer on a separate disc.

cards.heading: A noir story beyond Master Chief
cards.text: Despite reacquiring independence from Microsoft in 2007, Bungie was contractually committed to two more Halo games for the publisher. ODST was initially conceived as a downloadable story expansion for Halo 3 to produce in the lull between the game's completion and Halo: Reach (2010). Instead of featuring recognizable characters such as armored protagonist Master Chief, the developers focused on the ODSTs. Story director Joseph Staten penned a detective story utilizing film noir designs, settings, and characters. Composer Martin O'Donnell abandoned his previous Halo themes to create a quieter, jazz-influenced sound. During development, the planned expansion grew in scope to that of a full-sized game. Release marketing for the game included a tie-in comic, live-action trailers, and print and web advertisements.

cards.heading: Reception and The Master Chief Collection
cards.text: ODST received generally positive reviews, particularly for its atmosphere, music and approach to the story. Some critics questioned whether the short campaign and extras justified the price. It sold more than three million copies and led U.S. sales in September 2009. The campaign later joined Halo: The Master Chief Collection, followed by Firefight on its updated platforms.

main.title: Gran Turismo
main.summary: Gran Turismo is a 2009 sim racing video game by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable.

cards.heading: Gran Turismo
cards.text: Gran Turismo is a 2009 sim racing video game by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation Portable. The game was announced at Sony's E3 press conference on May 11, 2004, alongside the original PSP. Following five years of delays and speculation, during which it was variously known as Gran Turismo Portable, Gran Turismo 4 Mobile, Gran Turismo 5 Mobile and Gran Turismo 4.5, it made a reappearance at E3 on June 2, 2009, in playable form. It was released on October 1, 2009, as one of the launch titles for the new PSP Go. As of September 2017, Gran Turismo has sold 4.67 million units, making it one of the best-selling PlayStation Portable games. On June 1, 2010, the game was re-released as part of Sony's Greatest Hits budget line of video games.

main.title: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves
main.summary: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: The search for Shambhala
cards.text: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves is a 2009 action-adventure game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. It is the second game in the Uncharted series. Set two years after Uncharted: Drake's Fortune (2007), the story follows Nathan Drake, Chloe Frazer and Elena Fisher as they search for the Cintamani Stone and Shambhala while battling a militia led by Serbian war criminal Zoran Lazarević.

cards.heading: Developing Drake's second adventure
cards.text: Naughty Dog began developing Among Thieves after Drake's Fortune. Marco Polo's expeditions through Asia helped inspire the treasure hunt. An updated engine supported more elaborate motion capture and cinematic sequences, alongside online multiplayer for the first time in the series.

cards.heading: Reception and The Nathan Drake Collection
cards.text: Among Thieves received acclaim for its narrative, voice acting, graphics, technical achievements, and cinematic quality. It received Game of the Year accolades from numerous publications and award events, and is considered one of the most significant games for the seventh console generation and amongst the greatest video games ever made. It sold more than six million copies worldwide, and was re-released on PlayStation 4 as part of Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection. A sequel, Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception, was released in 2011.

main.title: Brütal Legend
main.subtitle: When Metal Becomes a Landscape
main.summary: Double Fine sends roadie Eddie Riggs into a heavy-metal fantasy where exploration and hand-to-hand action lead into strategic stage battles.

cards.heading: Eddie enters a metal world
cards.text: Double Fine released Br?tal Legend for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in North America on October 13, 2009. Tim Schafer's adventure follows roadie Eddie Riggs through a world of stages, amplifiers, engines and monsters drawn from heavy-metal imagery. Exploration and fighting combine with strategic battles, accompanied by a licensed repertoire of more than one hundred tracks.

cards.heading: The roadie becomes the hero
cards.text: Eddie brings the practical experience of a roadie into the fantasy. Preparing a show means understanding equipment and helping others perform, skills the game adapts to leading a force. Choosing a backstage worker as the protagonist also gives Schafer's comedy a character familiar with the work behind the spectacle.

cards.heading: Travelling through an album-cover landscape
cards.text: The landscape draws on the scale and imagery of metal album covers. Mountains, creatures and structures share their exaggerated shapes, while driving lets the soundtrack accompany exploration. The music and scenery establish the same setting through sound and appearance.

cards.heading: Commanding the stage battles
cards.text: Stage battles shift the focus towards commanding units and managing a wider conflict. Eddie continues to fight while coordinating activity around the stage. Double Fine acknowledged that this strategic direction surprised some players after the opening action sequences. The combination became one of the most debated parts of the game.

main.title: Machinarium
main.subtitle: Even Rust Can Be Gentle
main.summary: Amanita Design follows the small robot Josef through a hand-drawn city, with gestures, pictures and mechanical puzzles carrying the adventure.

cards.heading: Josef in the mechanical city
cards.text: Amanita Design released Machinarium for Windows, Mac and Linux on October 16, 2009. Josef, a small robot, explores a city of worn metal, mechanisms and discarded objects. Drawn animation, music and gestures convey the characters' intentions, while puzzles ask him to use the objects he can reach.

cards.heading: Reading gestures and pictures
cards.text: Characters communicate through pictures, gestures and short scenes. The player watches what an inhabitant is doing, then connects the request with nearby objects. Repeated movements or reactions can supply a clue before Josef has found the item needed to help.

cards.heading: Stretching and crouching
cards.text: Josef can stretch upward or crouch down. Changing his height lets him reach mechanisms or fit into confined spaces, so positioning matters when examining a room. An object visible on screen may require Josef to move closer or alter his body before he can use it.

cards.heading: The city and Floex's music
cards.text: Worn machines and hand-drawn details give the city a history beyond Josef's immediate journey. Floex's music accompanies its melancholy, danger and humour. Helping inhabitants and repairing objects supplies many of the small encounters that connect its rooms.

main.title: Borderlands
main.summary: Borderlands is a 2009 action role-playing first-person shooter video game developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K.

cards.heading: Vault Hunters reach Pandora
cards.text: Gearbox Software developed Borderlands, published by 2K in October 2009 for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Windows. Four Vault Hunters travel to Pandora in search of an alien Vault said to contain valuable technology. Following clues means fighting the planet's wildlife, bandits and the Atlas Corporation's forces.

cards.heading: Weapons, classes and cooperation
cards.text: The game features the ability to explore the in-game world, and complete both main missions and optional side quests, either in single-player or online cooperative gameplay, with the latter providing additional options for duels and competitive PVP matches in designated areas. Gameplay features include access to various weapons and shields that vary in type and statistics, weapons with special elemental functions, each playable character having distinctive class types and unique abilities for combat, upgradable skills, and the use of two-person vehicles. The game itself is rendered in cartoon-style graphics, to provide greater detail on weapons and environments, and was inspired by action role-playing games of the time, such as Ultima and Diablo.

cards.heading: Expansions and a continuing series
cards.text: Borderlands sold over two million copies by the end of 2009. Four expansions added new settings and challenges, including The Zombie Island of Dr. Ned and The Secret Armory of General Knoxx. Its success established a continuing series, with Borderlands 2 following in 2012. The original returned in an enhanced edition in 2019.

main.title: Forza Motorsport 3
main.summary: Forza Motorsport 3 is a 2009 racing video game developed for Xbox 360 by Turn 10 Studios.

cards.heading: A larger Forza garage
cards.text: Forza Motorsport 3 is a 2009 racing video game developed for Xbox 360 by Turn 10 Studios. It is the sequel to Forza Motorsport 2 and the third installment in the Forza series. The game includes more than 400 customizable cars (more than 500 cars in Ultimate Collection version) from 50 manufacturers and more than 100 racetrack variations with the ability to race up to eight cars on track at a time. These cars vary from production cars to race cars such as those from the American Le Mans Series.

cards.heading: Cockpit view and expanded car options
cards.text: New features include a cockpit view, assisted driving and vehicle rollovers. Players can paint and upgrade cars, with some production models capable of reaching racing classes through modifications. The game ships on two discs: one for play and another holding additional vehicles and tracks to install.

cards.heading: The season calendar
cards.text: A new single-player season mode puts the player through a completely personalized racing calendar that includes more than 200 different events, including circuit, oval, drag, drift, and timed events personalized to the player's tastes. New to the series are Circuit de la Sarthe and Circuit de Catalunya. These tracks join Road Atlanta, Road America, Twin Ring Motegi, Silverstone, Laguna Seca, Tsukuba, Mugello Circuit, Sebring International Raceway, Suzuka Circuit, and Nürburgring Nordschleife as the licensed real-world tracks included in the game.

cards.heading: Assists, storefronts and private race rules
cards.text: Driving assists can automate acceleration and braking, leaving the player to steer. These options open racing to people who cannot use the full controller. Online, the storefront lets players offer liveries, logos and tuning setups, while the auction house supports buying and selling cars. A rules editor allows groups to configure private multiplayer races.

cards.heading: Physics and replay tools
cards.text: The physics system adds tyre deformation and rollovers. Computer-controlled opponents can make mistakes under pressure, depending on the chosen difficulty. Photo and video tools let players record their cars and races, while separate leaderboards recognise driving, tuning and painting. Racing targets 60 frames per second.

cards.heading: Trying again with Rewind
cards.text: Rewind lets players reverse a recent section of a race to correct a mistake and try the corner or overtake again. The ability joins the other driving assists, giving players a way to practise a difficult moment without restarting the entire event.

cards.heading: Recording engines and tyres
cards.text: The sound team recorded cars and engines on chassis dynamometers, using consistent microphone placements and input settings. Tyre recordings on different surfaces help communicate the edge of grip. FMOD and custom code adjust effects such as pitch-related processing, panning, equalisation and volume in response to the car's physics.
